description: Django 2.2 project-management and issue-tracker application with kanban, Git integration, timelogs, and a custom search DSL. The six findings comprise one inherited stored-data ReDoS flow and five seeded flows integrated into existing application features.

vulnerabilities.description: The "test repository connection" endpoint reads `url` directly from `request.POST` and passes it to `Frontend.test_connection()`, which concatenates it into a `git ls-remote <url>` shell command with `shell=True`. Unlike the actual repository-create flow, this endpoint does not go through `RepositoryCreateForm`/the model's `validate_local_path` validator, so shell metacharacters in the URL are not blocked.
vulnerabilities.vulnerabilityImpact: Allows an authenticated developer to execute arbitrary OS commands with the privileges of the server process by supplying a URL containing shell metacharacters.

vulnerabilities.description: The "try a regex pattern" endpoint (a preview tool for building advanced searches) runs `re.match(pattern, sample)` with both the pattern and the sample text taken directly from the request body, and no timeout or length limit. A catastrophic-backtracking pattern like `(a+)+$` matched against a crafted sample hangs the worker.
vulnerabilities.vulnerabilityImpact: Allows an authenticated user to hang the single-threaded application worker with a single request, denying service to all other users.

vulnerabilities.description: The advanced search DSL's `~` comparator maps to Django's `__regex` ORM lookup (`comparatorToQExpression` in search/parser.py), so an attacker-controlled pattern such as `Issue.title ~ "(a+)+$"` is evaluated against every stored value of the targeted field when `SearchFrontend.query()` calls `.filter(expr)`. Unlike the `TestPatternView` sample-based variant, this one requires a stored value shaped to trigger catastrophic backtracking (a short, unrelated stored title does not manifest the hang) — confirmed live by first running a control query against the seed data (returned instantly) and then again after planting a long-titled issue (hung and timed out).
vulnerabilities.vulnerabilityImpact: Allows an authenticated user who can also create or control a searchable record (e.g. an issue title) to hang the single-threaded application worker for any other user who runs a matching regex search, or to hang it themselves on demand.

vulnerabilities.description: The quick issue-search endpoint's `q` query parameter is formatted directly into a raw SQL query executed via `django.db.connection.cursor()`, instead of being passed as a bound parameter.
vulnerabilities.vulnerabilityImpact: Allows an authenticated user to break out of the intended keyword filter and, via UNION-based injection, read data from other tables (e.g. other users' credentials) that the issue-search feature was never meant to expose.

vulnerabilities.description: The advanced issue-filter endpoint evaluates the caller-supplied `expression` with Python's `eval()`, passing only a local-variable context dict that does not restrict access to builtins.
vulnerabilities.vulnerabilityImpact: Allows an authenticated user to execute arbitrary Python code, and via `__import__`, arbitrary OS commands, on the server.

vulnerabilities.description: The timelog-report download endpoint joins a request-controlled `filename` parameter onto the project's export directory with no containment check before opening it, allowing `../` sequences to escape the intended per-project folder.
vulnerabilities.vulnerabilityImpact: Allows an authenticated user with read access to a project to read arbitrary files on the server outside the exports folder.
